usual_baseline: Mechanism of injury is usually well documented (86–100%). Skin, neurovascular and post-reduction checks are weaker: national BOAST 12 compliance 41.7% with neurovascular documentation 40.7% [1585]; skin 54–71% [1603, 1645]. Malreduction after fixation runs at 25–33% [1556, 1568]. Early weight-bearing after surgery is rare (10% [1603]).
fix_that_works: Education with infographic posters cut malreduction from 25% to 9.4% [1568]. A process change backed by education cut malreduction from 33% to 2.4% [1556]. Induction and trauma-meeting teaching lifted precise documentation from 17% to 88% [1645]. Posters and specialist teaching raised saved syndesmosis stress images from 55% to 82% [1701]. A protocol cut inappropriate fracture clinic referrals by 53% [1440].
fix_that_fails: Education and reflection alone did not help: malreduction rose to 43.8% at interim re-audit [1556]. One interactive plaster session plus posters did not significantly improve cast angle (27.7% to 37.7% acceptable, p=0.231), with only 3% gain where junior doctors were trained [1654]. The 'DNVI' shorthand persisted after teaching [1645].
consultant_advice: ED documentation of BOAST standards is heavily audited and usually improves with teaching. More useful is measuring outcome: malreduction on post-operative films, syndesmosis testing, or early weight-bearing and its documented reasons. Full BOAST 12 compliance was linked to earlier discharge [1585], so a bundle measure is worth tracking.
